snapshot.text: Wizz Air, the Central and Eastern European low-cost carrier, grew revenue by {{revenue.change@FY2026}} to {{revenue@FY2026}} in FY2026 while the Pratt & Whitney GTF engine issue continued to ground aircraft and constrain capacity, utilisation and cost performance.
The EBITDA margin widened by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2026}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2026}}, and net leverage fell by {{net_leverage.change@FY2026}} to {{net_leverage@FY2026}}.

The point to watch is leverage against peers: net leverage of {{net_leverage@FY2026}} is above the low-cost median of {{net_leverage.peer_median@FY2026}}, the weakest of the group ({{net_leverage.peer_rank@FY2026}}).

credit_metrics.text: EBITDA increased by {{ebitda.change@FY2026}} to {{ebitda@FY2026}}, but operating profit fell by {{operating_profit.change@FY2026}} to {{operating_profit@FY2026}} as depreciation, amortisation and impairment rose by {{dda.change@FY2026}} to {{dda@FY2026}}.

Total debt rose by {{total_debt.change@FY2026}} to {{total_debt@FY2026}} and net debt by {{net_debt.change@FY2026}} to {{net_debt@FY2026}}, yet gross leverage fell by {{gross_leverage.change@FY2026}} to {{gross_leverage@FY2026}} on the larger earnings base.

FFO rose by {{ffo.change@FY2026}} to {{ffo@FY2026}}, lifting FFO to debt by {{ffo_to_debt.change@FY2026}} to {{ffo_to_debt@FY2026}}, while interest coverage improved by {{interest_coverage.change@FY2026}} to {{interest_coverage@FY2026}} despite finance costs rising by {{finance_costs.change@FY2026}} to {{finance_costs@FY2026}}.

Free cash flow was broadly unchanged at {{fcf@FY2026}} as cash from operations rose by {{cfo.change@FY2026}} to {{cfo@FY2026}} and capex rose by {{capex.change@FY2026}} to {{capex@FY2026}}, so FCF to debt slipped by {{fcf_to_debt.change@FY2026}} to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2026}}.

operating_performance.text: Passengers rose by {{passengers.change@FY2026}} to {{passengers@FY2026}} on capacity up {{ask.change@FY2026}} to {{ask@FY2026}} available seat kilometres, with revenue passenger kilometres up {{rpk.change@FY2026}} to {{rpk@FY2026}}.
The load factor slipped by {{load_factor.change@FY2026}} to {{load_factor@FY2026}}, in line with the peer median of {{load_factor.peer_median@FY2026}}.

Unit revenue was stable, with RASK at {{rask@FY2026}} and passenger yield at {{passenger_yield@FY2026}}, while CASK was broadly unchanged at {{cask@FY2026}} as CASK ex-fuel rose by {{cask_ex_fuel.change@FY2026}} to {{cask_ex_fuel@FY2026}}.

Fuel cost was stable at {{fuel_cost@FY2026}} and its share of costs fell by {{fuel_share_of_costs.change@FY2026}} to {{fuel_share_of_costs@FY2026}}, above the peer median of {{fuel_share_of_costs.peer_median@FY2026}}.
The fleet grew by {{fleet.change@FY2026}} to {{fleet@FY2026}} aircraft with an average age of {{fleet_age@FY2026}}, and the company renegotiated its remaining Airbus order book, deferring deliveries.

liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments rose by {{cash_like.change@FY2026}} to {{cash_like@FY2026}}, taking cash liquidity to revenue up by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2026}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2026}}.

Customer prepayments grew: contract liabilities rose by {{contract_liabilities.change@FY2026}} to {{contract_liabilities@FY2026}}, and advance ticket cover rose by {{advance_ticket_cover.change@FY2026}} to {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2026}}, above the peer median of {{advance_ticket_cover.peer_median@FY2026}}.
The company repaid its eurobond out of free cash and renewed its Euro Medium Term Note programme, with Fitch and Moody's issuing ratings with stable and negative outlooks respectively.

peer_positioning.text: Wizz Air has the highest EBITDA margin of the low-cost group ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@FY2026}}), at {{ebitda_margin@FY2026}} against a median of {{ebitda_margin.peer_median@FY2026}}.

Leverage is the weakest part of the profile: gross leverage of {{gross_leverage@FY2026}} and net leverage of {{net_leverage@FY2026}} both rank last of the group ({{gross_leverage.peer_rank@FY2026}} and {{net_leverage.peer_rank@FY2026}}), against medians of {{gross_leverage.peer_median@FY2026}} and {{net_leverage.peer_median@FY2026}}.

Cash generation also trails the group, with FFO to debt of {{ffo_to_debt@FY2026}} and FCF to debt of {{fcf_to_debt@FY2026}} below medians of {{ffo_to_debt.peer_median@FY2026}} and {{fcf_to_debt.peer_median@FY2026}}, while cash liquidity to revenue sits in the middle of the group.

watch_items.text: Leverage: net leverage of {{net_leverage@FY2026}} is above the peer median of {{net_leverage.peer_median@FY2026}} and ranks last of the group ({{net_leverage.peer_rank@FY2026}}), leaving limited headroom against the low-cost peers.

Cash flow: FCF to debt fell by {{fcf_to_debt.change@FY2026}} to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2026}} as capex rose by {{capex.change@FY2026}} to {{capex@FY2026}}, and capex intensity increased by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2026}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2026}}.

Customer prepayments: advance ticket cover of {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2026}} is above the peer median of {{advance_ticket_cover.peer_median@FY2026}} and ranks last of the group ({{advance_ticket_cover.peer_rank@FY2026}}), so a larger share of liquidity is refundable to customers.
Costs: CASK ex-fuel rose by {{cask_ex_fuel.change@FY2026}} to {{cask_ex_fuel@FY2026}} while the GTF engine issue continued to affect capacity, utilisation and cost performance.
